findings.reason: the plan's own followup `f-otmp-dispatch-prebuild` names `capabilities.cached_pick_input` as the cache to key on, so §8's landed summary should cite that owner and the profile reader should call it rather than fork it.
findings.text: the run-time-profile cache re-implements the pick-input cache owner: `_read_persisted_profile` (lane_context.py:288), `_write_persisted_profile` (:310), `_profile_key` (:273), `_stat_stamp` (:237), `_ledger_stamp` (:252) and `_cached_run_time_profile` (:337) hand-roll a schema-marked, atomic, stamp-keyed persisted cache that `reckon/capabilities.py:1193 cached_pick_input` (with `capabilities.file_stamp` at :1149) already provides, using a second `_store.cache_root` kind (`run-time-profile`) beside the `pick-input` kind, so the version-mismatch and corrupt-entry handling now has two implementations that must stay in step.

findings.reason: extend `run_time_profile._size_class` and `local_lane_load` as the single owner of size classification and lane reading and delete the re-derived copies, so one threshold change has one site.
findings.text: `_bucket` duplicates `reckon/crew/run_time_profile.py:172 _size_class`: both classify a node by the same declared-budget thresholds (30/60 min) falling back to output tokens (<20k/<=100k) and return the same `BUDGET_KEY`/`OUTPUT_SIZE_KEY` bucket names imported from `run_time_profile`; the same census covers `_number` at lane_context.py:65, run_time_profile.py:79 and picker/outcomes.py:39, `_percentile` at run_time_profile.py:100 and picker/outcomes.py:46, and `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:464`, which re-reads the lane document that `run_time_profile.local_lane_load()` (run_time_profile.py:382), which it already calls, has just read (`snapshot._lane` is a third reader of the same document).

findings.reason: the section must state, in its own text, which option, view, definition or refusal family the new picker surface retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
findings.text: the section adds interface surface without accounting for it: the picker ships the `crew pick` verb (`reckon/cli.py:1433`, fifteen options including `--replay`, `--outcomes`, `--all-projects`) and adds `--route` and `--comment` to `crew dispatch` (`reckon/cli.py:1664`), a real addition to the cli_options family (317), while §5 and §6 name no CLI option, MCP view, public definition or refusal family they retire or merge and give no reason none can be; no picker view was added to the mcp_views family (stays 33) and no new refusal family was added (refusal_families stays 23, `D01`–`D23`), and §1's merge of backend definitions (claude with `claude-opus`/`claude-haiku`, the codex variants) belongs to none of the four counted families.

response_events.reason: crew pick and dispatch --route/--comment are the picker's whole interface and no existing surface does what they do: the deterministic route stays as the picker's fallback, so nothing can be retired. The surface does shrink in the locked lane-and-model redesign, which folds per-model backends such as claude-opus into one lane per subscription.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `pick()` at `reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:47` is one entry point hiding the candidate snapshot, the Jev call, the Jinja state render, the answer validation and the fallback behind a `PickRequest`→`Selection` interface (`types.py`), so substantial behaviour sits behind a small surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py` forks the picker-input cache and the run-time-profile reader that `reckon/capabilities.py` and `reckon/crew/run_time_profile.py` already own.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1489, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §5 and §6 add the `crew pick` verb and the `dispatch --route` and `--comment` options (cli_options) and the picker package's public definitions without either section naming what it retires or merges, or stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §4's `picker-reuse-map` node mapped 28 base-revision functions before building, and the implementation honours it: `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py` adapts the existing hard gates (`budget.preflight`, `_lane_worker_allowance`, `_dispatch_lane_gate`, `routing._competence_verdict`, `recovery._review_excluded_backends`, `resumption.probe_lane_availability`, `_store.cache_root`) rather than re-deriving eligibility.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the picker is not a thin layer over an existing selector; it adds the Jev judgment (§10) that deterministic `routing.resolve_role_override` does not carry, and reuses the deterministic gates rather than re-implementing them.
